drills.label: Cold open
drills.question_line: SAM: Here is your opening item. An operations lead at a logistics firm
drills.stem: An operations lead wants Claude to speed up a weekly supplier-performance report: an analyst pulls figures from three spreadsheets, writes commentary, a manager checks it, and it goes to the procurement director. What should the operations lead do first?

options.A: Have Claude draft the commentary every week from now on
options.B: Ask Claude to design a new report format and switch next week
options.C: Map steps, times and error points; pick the step, keep the manager's check, pilot against the current report
options.D: Hand it to IT to build an automated pipeline across the three sources

drills.why: Nobody has measured where the hours or errors are. Mapping the current process gives a baseline and points Claude at the right step, with the manager's check kept.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. An H R partner has interview notes from five managers
drills.answer_line: SAM: B. Claude does the reading and sorting
drills.stem: An HR partner has notes from five managers about a new onboarding process. Two want laptops ready on day one, two say the first week is fine, one never mentions equipment. What is the best use of Claude?

options.A: Have Claude write the final requirements, resolving the disagreements
options.B: Extract each manager's needs, flag conflicts and gaps, draft follow-up questions, confirm with the managers
options.C: Use only the most senior manager's notes
options.D: Ask Claude which managers are right

drills.why: Claude does the reading and sorting; the people who own the process settle the conflict. The silent manager is a gap to ask about.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. Choose two. A consultant is preparing a client deck
drills.answer_line: SAM: A is right. C is the trusting-the-model's-confidence distractor
drills.stem: A consultant preparing a client deck on entering a new regional market needs current competitor and regulation information. Which two steps are most appropriate?

options.A: Use research mode for a multi-source, cited report
options.B: Check key figures and regulatory claims against the cited sources
options.C: Ask Claude to rate its confidence and keep only high-confidence claims
options.D: Paste the client's confidential pricing model into a personal account
options.E: Use a fast model with web search off to save time

drills.why: Research mode fits a many-source, cited question, and citations make checking possible, not unnecessary. A model's rating of its own answer is not evidence.

drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. On the exam this comes as four statements
drills.answer_line: ALEX: One, yourself. Two, reviewer. Three, escalate. Four, yourself.
drills.prompt: For each, choose: do it yourself with Claude; do it with a named reviewer before it goes out; or escalate to an Architect or Developer. 1. Summarise your own notes from yesterday's internal workshop. 2. Draft a customer notice about a price change. 3. Have Claude's replies post automatically into the customer system with nobody in between. 4. Build an artifact mock-up of a new expense form for feedback.
drills.answer: 1. Yourself: internal, low stakes. 2. Named reviewer: customer-facing commercial commitment. 3. Escalate: integration with a company system, human removed. 4. Yourself: a prototype meant to be critiqued.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A sales lead's team spends about three hours
drills.answer_line: SAM: Right. A redesigns what the stem says works.
drills.stem: A sales team spends about three hours per account writing summaries before each quarterly business review. The rest of the review process works well. What is the best way to bring Claude in?

options.A: Redesign the whole review process around Claude first
options.B: Project with the template; Claude drafts from account notes, rep reviews; compare time against three hours
options.C: Stop writing summaries; Claude answers questions live in the meeting
options.D: Wait for a full sales-system integration

drills.why: One slow step in a working process: augment that step, keep the rep's review, and measure against the baseline.

drills.label: Drill
drills.question_line: SAM: Pause here and answer before we go on. A finance director asks whether Claude can prepare
drills.answer_line: SAM: C. It sells the real value
drills.scenario: Finance director wants no more checking
drills.stem: A finance director asks whether Claude can prepare month-end variance commentary automatically, so the team can stop checking it. What is the best response?

options.A: Yes, Claude is accurate enough that checking is no longer needed
options.B: No, AI should not be used near financial reporting
options.C: Claude drafts and flags unusual movements; the team still checks and signs off; pilot measuring time saved
options.D: Tell the director to raise it with IT

drills.why: Sell the real value and keep the control where the accountability sits. A overpromises; B abandons the task; D passes on a business question.

drills.question_line: SAM: Your turn first. Pause and name the five tasks we covered, and the habit that wins each one. [pause]
drills.answer_line: ALEX: Requirements: surface conflicts, don't settle them.
drills.prompt: Name the five tasks we covered, and the habit that wins each one.
drills.answer: Requirements: surface conflicts, don't settle them. Research and process: real detail, check sources. Design: prototype, then escalate. Augment or redesign: match change to pain, with a baseline. Stakeholders: value, limits and controls together.

In this episode: Research mode and real process detail
Augment one step, or redesign the process
Explain value and limits to a sponsor
Cold open: the weekly report: 5 tasks: requirements, research and planning, design, workflows, stakeholders
Understand the work before changing it
Keep a human where accountability sits
Distractors rush to automate or refuse to start
Requirements and use cases: Claude extracts needs, who raised them, conflicts and gaps
A finished-looking document reads as settled
A strawman draft is real, but not when inputs conflict
Use-case fit: language work, repeats, checkable, has what it needs
Final sign-off on a payment run is a person's
Research, planning and process optimisat: Quick fact: chat with web search
Many sources, compared and cited: research mode
Citations make checking possible, not unnecessary
Plans need the real deadline, team and constraints
The detail you give is the ceiling on the advice
Supporting design and iteration: Several options, critique against criteria, artifacts to react to
Small tested steps, one change at a time
Associates escalate complex or technical work
Company systems, autonomy, every customer, the API: Architects and Developers
A working prototype is the best brief
Augment or redesign: Augment: Claude takes one step in a process that stays
Pain in one step vs pain in handoffs and rework
Over-reviewing kills adoption; over-redesigning is overspend
Communicating value and limits: Value in their terms, measured against the baseline
Limits: confidently wrong, knowledge boundaries, drafts people own
Some decisions stay with a person
A sponsor who finds limits later feels misled
Pair each limit with its control
Cold open: the verdict: Answer: C, map steps, times and error points, then pilot
Nobody has measured where the hours or errors are
A jumps to a fix with no before and after
B redesigns the output; D escalates what needs no integration
Five to remember: Claude surfaces conflicts; process owners settle them
Research mode for cited multi-source questions; check the sources; feed real process detail
Prototype yourself; escalate systems, autonomy and production
Augment a slow step, redesign broken handoffs; baseline, checkpoint, pilot
Measured value, every limit paired with a control; never promise no checking
Recap: the exam tells: Notes disagree → flag the conflict, take it to the owners
"Specific to our process" → give Claude steps, times, handoffs
Filter by Claude's confidence → distractor; check the cited source
One slow step → augment; handoffs and rework → redesign
Sponsor wants "no errors" → value, limit and control together
"First" → map and measure the current process
